source.label: Office of Gov. Tate Reeves, "Governor Reeves Announces 167 Rural Health Transformation Program Awards Totaling More Than $104 Million" (Sept 14, 2026)

rows.purpose: To modernize aging technology that will strengthen operational sustainability and expand access to high-quality behavioral healthcare.
To replace an outdated and unreliable electronic door access system to better protect patients, staff and facility operations.
To implement new technology tools that will improve documentation efficiency, automate eligibility verification and improve interoperability.
To modernize technology to create a secure, integrated and interoperable environment for rural health delivery.
To update technology across three outpatient clinics including upgraded workstations, self-check-in kiosks, collaboration technology and workflow software.

To add a tertiary cellular wireless wide-area network (WAN) connection at 67 rural satellite clinics that will preserve electronic health records access, strengthen infrastructure resilience and cybersecurity, and maintain rural continuity during fiber disruptions.

To replace six disconnected phone systems with unified cloud-hosted VoIP platform and standardize fragmented access control and video surveillance systems with centralized, secure and more reliable technology.
To deploy ambient AI documentation to approximately 500 providers across its multispecialty network to reduce documentation burden, provider burnout and after-hours charting.
To implement modern pediatric electronic health records with AI-enabled clinical documentation, patient engagement tools and population health capabilities.

To add AI-native email and browser threat detection layer beyond its existing secure email gateway which will help identify sophisticated attacks such as business email compromise, lookalike-domain fraud, QR-code phishing and malicious links that traditional gateway tools may miss.
To upgrade an automated medication dispensing system and badge security access control system which will improve medication accountability, patient safety and physical security.
To establish a physically segregated, air gapped recovery environment with immutable storage, dedicated identity controls and malware scanning.

rows.recipient: Mississippi Children’s Home Society dba Canopy Children’s Solutions
rows.purpose: To design a modern enterprise data infrastructure that will support interoperability by creating an enterprise data strategy, governance framework and a phased roadmap to strengthen long-term infrastructure to better serve 14,000 children across 82 counties.

To install current-generation high-availability firewalls with advanced threat protection, URL filtering and full implementation services to store supported perimeter security, reduce HIPAA and cybersecurity risk and protect care delivery across more than 60 ambulatory sites.

To implement a secure, one-click interoperability solution that retrieves complete patient records for referring rural electronic health records and integrate those records into the Center’s surgical platform.

To support the Mobile Health Bridge program that combines remote patient monitoring tools with in-home visits by community paramedics and a transitional care nurse. Enables real-time biometric tracking, physical assessments, point-of-care testing and digital documentation in patients’ homes.

To upgrade servers, networks, endpoint devices, cybersecurity, identity and access management and backup and disaster recovery capabilities to reduce downtime, improve reliability and better protect patient information.

To modernize the clinic’s technology to include digital intake tablets, ambient listening tools for automated documentation, exam-room technology upgrades to increase patient capacity, improve efficiency and patient experience and help the clinic’s limited specialist workforce serve more rural patients effectively.

To modernize electronic medical records for 50 rural Mississippi healthcare practices. This will help rural providers meet new CMS interoperability and prior authorization requirements by adding enhanced tools to reduce manual and fax-based processes, improve care coordination and data exchange and support faster, more informed patient care across rural communities.
To modernize the Ocean Springs primary care hub, strengthen cybersecurity and establish three new rural sites, creating a secure four-site network.

rows.recipient: Southeast Mississippi Rural Health Initiative, Inc
rows.purpose: To modernize clinical technology by replacing endpoint devices and redesigning its deployment strategy to improve efficiency, cybersecurity and long-term sustainability.

To replace outdated computers with 15 laptops with docking stations and 15 desktops to ensure reliable compatibility with clinic’s electronic health records system, telehealth platform, billing and other essential healthcare systems.

To modernize critical IT infrastructure, which will replace outdated network, server, storage, backup and endpoint systems, add 24/7 security information and event management monitoring and implement a hospital-wide security camera system to strengthen both cyber and physical security.

To purchase Diagnostic Cardiology Suite software and three compatible laptops to expand EKG capacity, improve integration with electronic health records system and reduce turnaround times for test results.
To modernize technology by purchasing laptops, which will replace outdated desktops to improve operational efficiency, support staff mobility and strengthen data security.

To replace outdated workstations and server equipment, add battery backup and cooling systems, and support compatibility with AI software to enhance diagnostics, treatment planning and workflow efficiency.
To modernize devices, implement secure-based collaboration and identity systems, and enhance cybersecurity and data protection across five district offices.

rows.recipient: Aaron E Henry Community Health Services Center, INC
rows.purpose: To modernize technology by replacing aging computers, implement AI-assisted documentation tools, enhance digital registration and patient engagement, and strengthen reporting capabilities to improve efficiency.
To purchase new workstations, tablets, wireless networking, telehealth tools and self-service kiosks.

rows.recipient: East Central Mississippi Health Care, Inc.
rows.purpose: To deploy remote patient monitoring technology for 1,300 patients with hypertension and other chronic conditions.

To strengthen cybersecurity by adding firewalls, purchasing managed detection and response software, creating an incident response plan, and provide staff training while also advancing AI and data capabilities.

To modernize technology in the clinic by implementing modern servers, upgraded devices and network equipment, centralized security monitoring, and professional migration support to better protect health information of approximately 31,700 rural patients.
To enhance network protections by replacing outdated servers and workstations, deploying enterprise endpoint protections and completing a HIPAA Security Risk Assessment with a corrective action plan.

rows.recipient: GA Carmichael Family Health Center, Inc.
rows.purpose: To upgrade critical technology infrastructure across its health center and school-based locations in six counties by investing in new workstations and stronger server and network infrastructure.
To implement managed threat detection and response tools, conduct an independent security risk assessment and penetration test, develop and test an incident-response plan, and provide staff training.
To purchase equipment and provide personnel to expand the preventive screening and remote patient monitoring across 5 primary care sites and 1 mobile clinic.

To modernize IT infrastructure by replacing unsupported network and wireless systems, migrate legacy servers, and move The Women’s Clinic onto hospital-owned secure infrastructure while replacing aging clinical technology.
To replace the facility’s end-of-life nurse call infrastructure and add integrated wandering protection for residents with dementia and other cognitive impairments.

To replace manual chemotherapy order transcription with standardized electronic oncology workflow program, which will improve patient safety, reduce errors and delays, and add clinical decision support for dosing and drug interaction review.

To modernize critical IT infrastructure for four critical access hospitals and one nursing home, which will enable telehealth deployment in emergency and inpatient rooms and prepare patient rooms for Smart Room capabilities.
To replace legacy voicemail refill systems with VOXO AI Pharmacy Voice Agent, which will allow patients to have 24/7 conversational support.

To implement a new breast milk management system that will use barcode verification, real-time validation and end-to-end tracking to improve neonatal safety, standardize workflows and support future expansion across maternal-child services.

To implement a nurse call system enhancement project that will add five nurse call master control stations and an audio expansion board to improve patient-caregiver communication, reduce response times and strengthen patient safety.
To equip two existing sleep study rooms with modern, compliant diagnostic equipment.

To implement an intelligent document intake platform radiology service, which will automate referral processing by digitizing inbound orders, extracting structured clinical data, and integrating with scheduling and electronic health records systems.

rows.recipient: The Mississippi Methodist Hospital and Rehabilitation Center, Inc
rows.purpose: To fund an Enterprise Cybersecurity Modernization and Resilience Initiative that will replace hardware and software to strengthen cybersecurity, improve operational resilience and protect continuity of specialized rehabilitation services statewide.
To enhance cybersecurity protections by purchasing equipment to modernize the network and servers, SD-WAN for remote clinics and manage SIEM monitoring.
To launch a clinical communication transformation program to integrate telephony, paging, secure messaging, EHR alerts, call lights and monitoring systems in real-time.

To create a shared, cloud-based analytics and reporting platform for participating rural hospitals to provide for a common reporting model, improve visibility into patient access and utilization, and build a sustainable data infrastructure to support better healthcare access and outcomes for rural Mississippians.

To implement a Delta Cardiovascular Connectivity Network, a centralized cardiology PACS and interoperability project that will enable centralized image access, structured reporting, remote-ready physician connectivity and dashboard monitoring.

rows.recipient: The Mississippi Methodist Hospital and Rehabilitation Center, Inc
rows.purpose: To modernize medication management by integrating a comprehensive platform into its existing electronic health records system.

To modernize key systems, including the nurse call system, patient monitoring technology and infant security system to strengthen patient communication, real-time clinical response and newborn protection.

To purchase equipment for an alerting thermostat system that will provide continuous, automated temperature monitoring in critical areas and send real-time alerts when conditions fall outside safe ranges.
To purchase equipment for a new electronic faxing solution to modernize rural hospital’s communication by replacing outdated, paper-based fax processes.

To replace the nurse call system with a modernized system and real-time location services platform, which will improve communications reliability, reduce maintenance concerns and strengthen the hospital’s care delivery infrastructure.

To implement a unified enterprise data warehouse and modern decision support platform integrating core systems, automating reporting and providing analytics for costing, productivity, quality and service line performance.
To purchase automated CPR technology.
To purchase equipment for an automated blood bank system.
To implement bi-directional integration between infusion pumps and Epic across four rural hospitals, while also replacing pumps at three of the sites.

To fund the purchase of equipment for Secure Clinical Access Platform Modernization to improve virtual desktop infrastructure, replace unsupported shared clinical endpoints and implement modern identity and single sign-on tools across its rural hospitals and clinics.
To launch a remote patient monitoring program for 400 patients with hypertension and diabetes across three rural clinics.
To modernize technology by replacing aging hardware and strengthening cybersecurity.
To implement a cloud-based ERP system that will modernize financial, supply chain and administrative operations.
To modernize the bed management process, improve interoperability and reduce manual workflows.
To strengthen the facility’s cybersecurity infrastructure.
To create a scalable and resilient digital ecosystem supporting high-quality healthcare delivery.
To reduce technology barriers that limit communication between rural providers and patients.
To modernize critical technology infrastructure supporting three rural clinics and a 120-bed skilled nursing facility.
To fund the implementation of a new enterprise clinical information system.
